definitions.gloss: casual speech, informal language between equals
definitions.explanation: Informal, plain-form speech used between people of equal status (same age, close friends, etc.). Contrasted with {敬語|けいご} (polite/formal language).

examples.english: You can talk to me casually.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先輩|せんぱい}→先輩：01451_senpai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧タメ{語|ご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{失礼|しつれい}→失礼：01247_shitsurei⟧だ。
examples.english: Using casual speech with a senior is rude.

examples.japanese: ⟦{同|おな}い{年|どし}→同い年：10051_onaidoshi⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧わかった⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、タメ{語|ご}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}り{替|か}えた→切り替える：04239_kirikaeru⟧。
examples.english: Once I found out we were the same age, I switched to casual speech.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
タメ comes from gambling slang where タメ means "equal" (as in dice showing the same number). ⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧ means "language/speech." So タメ{語|ご} literally means "equal-status language."

USAGE:
The shift from ⟦{敬語|けいご}→敬語：04022_keigo⟧ to タメ{語|ご} is an important social milestone in Japanese relationships. Being invited to use タメ{語|ご} signals closeness and acceptance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- タメ{語|ご}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧: to speak casually
- タメ{語|ご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧: to use casual speech
- タメ{語|ご}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}り{替|か}える→切り替える：04239_kirikaeru⟧: to switch to casual speech
- タメ{語|ご}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧: casual speech is fine
